comparisons.peer_topic: Allowance for Credit Losses Trends and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: The allowance for credit losses for loans and lending commitments remained relatively unchanged in 2024, driven by provisions for specific commercial real estate loans and corporate loan growth, offset by charge-offs mainly in the office sector and an improved macroeconomic outlook.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS disclose the drivers behind changes in their Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) or outstanding loans in 2024. BAC reports a significant $41.4 billion increase in outstanding loans and leases, primarily driven by $36.4 billion in commercial portfolio growth. In contrast, MS reports that its ACL for loans and lending commitments remained relatively unchanged in 2024, with specific drivers including provisions for certain commercial real estate loans and growth in the corporate loan portfolio, offset by charge-offs. While BAC focuses on balance sheet expansion in the commercial segment, MS highlights offsetting forces (provisions vs. charge-offs/macro outlook) leading to stability in its credit reserve, indicating different risk and growth dynamics in their commercial/real estate exposures.

sentences.text: Outstanding loans and leases excluding loans accounted for under the fair value option increased $41.4 billion in 2024 primarily driven by commercial, which increased $36.4 billion due to broad-based growth.

The allowance for credit losses for loans and lending commitments was relatively unchanged in 2024, reflecting provisions for certain specific commercial real estate loans and growth in the corporate loan portfolio, offset by charge-offs related to commercial real estate lending, mainly in the office sector, and improvements in the macroeconomic outlook.
